title: Typography — Kerning, OpenType Features & Exact Metrics

metadata.author: pdfnative-cli samples
metadata.subject: kerning, fontFeatures (onum, smcp, pnum), metrics exact (pdfnative 1.8.0)
metadata.keywords: typography, kerning, opentype, small caps, old-style figures

blocks.text: kerning: true applies the font's pair-kerning table (kern / GPOS) so letter pairs such as AV, WA, To, Ye and VA sit closer: AVAWAY To Ye VA WAVE Tommy Yves. fontFeatures lists OpenType single-substitution features the renderer applies to every run set in a registered font: onum turns 0123456789 into old-style figures, smcp sets lowercase letters as small capitals, pnum requests proportional figures.

Invoice 2026-041, order 0917, reference 3854-1207, quantity 12, total 1450. Old-style figures share the x-height of the lowercase and descend below the baseline, which reads better inside running text.
Names and acronyms set in small capitals: nasa, unesco, iso 15930-7, pdf/x-4 — the lowercase letters become small caps, the capitals stay as they are.

metrics: "exact" replaces the approximate width table of the standard-14 fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier) with the Adobe Core 14 AFM metrics, so lines set in a base-14 font wrap exactly where a viewer measures them. It changes nothing for a registered font such as Noto Sans, which carries its own advance widths.

Tip: request tnum or lnum with Noto Sans and the TYPOGRAPHY_FEATURE_INEFFECTIVE diagnostic tells you the font already uses tabular lining figures — the tag changes nothing. Under --strict that diagnostic fails the render.
